OK everybody, we're going on a class trip to Lee Castle next week, so I'd like to tell you a bit about the castle.

The oldest parts of it were built in the 11th century, a time when there were lots of battles in the area. But following a fire in the 12th century, most of it had to be built again. This didn't happen until the 13th century.

As you know, people generally made their buildings from wood. After all, much of the area is covered in trees even now. Building with stone wasn't easy, so the fact it was used here shows how important this castle was. It was much stronger than buildings made using earth, which was also common back then.

When we finished in the castle, we'll go outside to the picnic area. While we're there enjoying the castle's beautiful garden, try and imagine the land as a farm. That's how it was used to provide food for people in the castle.

Finally, after lunch there'll be a quiz to see who in the class remembers most about what you saw during the tour. So pay attention to the guide and also remember to make notes during the film you'll see when we first arrive.

The last owner of the castle was an interesting man and I'd like you to find out something about him for homework. His name was William Hazworth, That's HAI SWORTH, you can look up some information online.
